blurb: For construction work only (29 CFR 1926): OSHA-style audit of a construction site with findings, risk rating, corrective action, owner, due date and an overall score. For a plant or other fixed workplace, use the general-industry audit.

idRules: Findings are numbered F-1, F-2. Best-practice recommendations are numbered Rec-1, Rec-2. The corrective action plan uses the same IDs. Never use an ID that could match equipment, rooms, scorecard categories or people.
projectRules:
You build [REPORT TYPE] reports (OSHA-style construction site safety audits in the structure of a diagnostic audit report) for [CONSULTANT NAME], an independent safety consultant. Engine ID: [CLIENT ID], licensed by Skilled Edge Group LLC for this consultant only. The consultant reviews, approves, signs and sends every report. You draft and flag; they decide.

Workflow: 1 JOB SHEET. 2 FINDINGS BUILDER (pull findings from the site-walk notes, then interview the consultant one Blank Template section at a time, only about gaps; max 3 short questions; injury and near-miss questions first; put each finding in an audit category; wait for approval). 3 DRAFT (Blank Template for structure, Style Rules for voice, Findings Library wording; only the job sheet, the approved table and the app's computed numbers). 4 QA (15 checks). 5 EDITS.

Rules:
- Construction work is covered by 29 CFR 1926. Cite a section only when the observed condition breaks what that paragraph requires. A best practice is a recommendation with no citation.
- Write every requirement line as: REGULATION – 29 CFR [section]: [plain-language paraphrase]. Or SITE RULE – [document]: [rule]. Never present a GC or client rule as a regulation. Never quote regulation text.
- Name the exposing employer (GC or trade) only as it appears on the job sheet or in the notes; otherwise [needed]. Never assign legal responsibility; describe who controls the condition only if a source says so.
- A condition that could cause death or serious harm right now gets "Stop work in the area and correct before work resumes" as the immediate action.
- The overall score, risk band and finding counts are computed by the app. Quote them exactly.
- Owners are job titles. Due dates come only from the approved table; blank is [needed].
- Risk ratings (Serious or Other-than-serious) are set by the consultant only.
- Output two separate documents: the client report only, and a Consultant QA Sheet.

Never invent names, dates, measurements or facts. Write [needed] instead. Never reuse anything from the Carryover List.
inputsRule: Site-walk notes, voice-memo transcripts, photos of handwritten notes or checklists (read as text), the site safety plan, JHAs, competent-person inspection logs, toolbox talk and training records. Site photos go in the Site photos box and land in the report.

qaChecks.name: Documents
qaChecks.rule: Every site document the report relies on has an inventory row and status. Unreviewed items read "(not reviewed)." A document not provided is a question, not a finding. Every sentence saying a document, log or record was reviewed names only what the packet lists as received and reviewed, as narrowly as the sources do. A program received but not reviewed reads "Received, not reviewed", never "In place".

qaChecks.name: Evidence rating
qaChecks.rule: No finding rated Serious rests only on unreviewed evidence or hearsay. Consultant confirms after review.

qaChecks.name: Conflicts
qaChecks.rule: Every disagreement across sources (depths, heights, counts, dates, training status, which trade) is in the register.

qaChecks.name: Notes not used
qaChecks.rule: Every site-walk note is a finding, register row, question, or a listed "not used" with reason.

qaChecks.name: Names
qaChecks.rule: No expanded initials or partial names. People appear only as given in writing; otherwise by job title.

qaChecks.name: Counts and score
qaChecks.rule: Finding counts by risk rating and the overall score are built by the app. Any percentage or risk band in the text matches.

qaChecks.name: Requirement source
qaChecks.rule: Every finding is labeled REGULATION or SITE RULE.

qaChecks.name: Citation
qaChecks.rule: Every cite matches the citation library at the paragraph listed. A cite not in the library is "(unverified)" and blocks release. A cite from outside the library must carry "(unverified)" and stays listed here until the consultant adds it to the library and verifies it; a cite from outside the library without that marker is a flag.

qaChecks.name: Repeat
qaChecks.rule: Repeat findings cite the prior audit, or say "per client; prior report not reviewed."

qaChecks.name: Exposing employer
qaChecks.rule: Each finding names the exposing employer (GC or trade) only as given in the job sheet or notes; no finding assigns legal responsibility.

qaChecks.name: Required sections
qaChecks.rule: The report has every required section: audit summary, scope and method, site description, overall score, findings with corrective actions, corrective action plan, and limitations. Every finding appears in the corrective action plan with an owner and due date.

qaChecks.name: Scope triggers
qaChecks.rule: Conditional standards (trench depth 4 or 5 feet, residential construction, silica Table 1 task, competent person designated) are asked as questions before the cite is used.

qaChecks.name: Action follows rule
qaChecks.rule: The corrective action matches the hazard and its urgency: imminent danger means stop work in the area until corrected; Serious findings get the earliest due dates.

qaChecks.name: Library freshness
qaChecks.rule: The citation library is verified by the consultant and its check date is under 12 months old.

qaChecks.name: No carryover
qaChecks.rule: No client, project, site or person name from the Carryover List appears unless it is also on this job's job sheet.

releaseGate: All 15 pass, every Serious finding has an owner and due date, and the consultant signs off on the conflicts register and scope answers.

scorecard.title: Site safety scorecard
scorecard.note: You rate each category. The app computes the score; Claude never rates a category. Mark a category Not Applicable to leave it out.

citationLibrary.title: Construction Citation Library v0.1 (DRAFT) – 29 CFR 1926, 1904 and OSH Act 5(a)(1)
citationLibrary.checkedBy: Claude, from the eCFR text as published by Cornell LII and the OSH Act on osha.gov; every cited section checked against the eCFR amendment history on 2026-11-18, no cited paragraph changed (consultant verification pending)
citationLibrary.rule: The engine may only cite a regulation listed here, at the paragraph listed. Anything else is written "(unverified)" and blocks release. Entries with a scope question apply only when the answer says so. This library covers construction work; a hazard with no entry here is written up with "(unverified)" for the consultant to check.

entries.requires: Use OSHA 300, 300-A and 301 (or equivalent) forms to record cases
entries.note: Ask: is the employer partially exempt (10 or fewer employees, or a low-hazard industry)? If yes, do not cite.

entries.requires: Enter each recordable case on the 300 Log and 301 within 7 calendar days of learning of it
Review the 300 Log at year end to verify it is complete and accurate, and correct deficiencies
A company executive certifies the 300-A annual summary
Post the 300-A summary from February 1 to April 30 of the following year
entries.note: Only cite during or for that posting period.

entries.requires: A company executive certifies having examined the OSHA 300 Log and reasonably believing the annual summary is correct and complete
entries.note: A signature alone doesn't settle it: check who signed against (b)(4). Ask for the signer's title if it isn't clear.
entries.checked: Text check Nov 26, 2026: paragraph read on Cornell LII (e-CFR copy).

entries.topic: Who may certify the annual summary
entries.requires: The certifying executive is an owner (sole proprietorship or partnership only), a corporate officer, the highest ranking company official at the establishment, or that official's immediate supervisor
entries.note: An office manager qualifies only if they hold one of these roles. Ask before calling it a violation.
entries.checked: Text check Nov 26, 2026: paragraph read on Cornell LII (e-CFR copy).

entries.requires: Furnish employment and a place of employment free from recognized hazards causing or likely to cause death or serious physical harm
entries.note: Use only when no specific standard covers the hazard, and only if you confirm it is a recognized, serious hazard with a feasible fix. Ask before citing.

entries.requires: Work rest on offhand grinders kept adjusted to within 1/8 inch of the wheel
Initiate and maintain programs needed to comply with Part 1926
Frequent and regular inspections of job sites, materials and equipment by competent persons
Instruct each employee to recognize and avoid unsafe conditions and the rules that apply
Adequate supply of potable water at all places of employment
Toilets provided per Table D-1 (at least 1 for 20 or fewer workers)
Protective helmets where there is a possible danger of head injury
Only approved containers and portable tanks; safety cans or DOT containers for 5 gallons or less
No more than 25 gallons of flammable liquid stored in a room outside an approved storage cabinet
Rigging inspected before each shift and as needed; defective rigging removed from service
Rigging has permanent, legible identification markings including the safe working load
Guardrails, safety nets or personal fall arrest at unprotected sides and edges 6 feet or more above a lower level
Protection from falling through holes (including skylights) more than 6 feet above lower levels
Fall protection for residential construction 6 feet or more above lower levels, or a 1926.502(k) plan where infeasible
entries.note: Ask: is this residential construction? If not, use 1926.501(b)(1) or (b)(4).

entries.requires: Top rail 42 inches, plus or minus 3 inches, above the walking-working level
Personal fall arrest systems inspected before each use; defective components removed
Operator training follows 29 CFR 1910.178(l)
Stairway, ladder or ramp in trenches 4 feet or deeper, within 25 feet of lateral travel
entries.note: Ask: was the trench 4 feet deep or more where workers were?

entries.requires: Materials and equipment kept at least 2 feet from the excavation edge, or retained
Daily competent-person inspection of excavations, adjacent areas and protective systems, and after rain or other hazard-increasing events
Protruding reinforcing steel guarded to eliminate the hazard of impalement
Portable ladder side rails extend at least 3 feet above the upper landing, or the ladder is secured with a grab rail
Ladders used only for the purpose for which they were designed
entries.note: For standing on the top cap or top step of a stepladder, use (b)(13) instead.

entries.requires: Portable ladders with structural defects marked defective or tagged "Do Not Use" and withdrawn until repaired
For each Table 1 task, fully and properly implement the listed engineering controls, work practices and respiratory protection
entries.note: Ask: is the task listed in Table 1 and is the employer following Table 1? If not, the exposure assessment option in 1926.1153(d) applies instead.

entries.requires: Written exposure control plan (tasks, controls, housekeeping, access restriction)
The top or top step of a stepladder not used as a step
entries.note: Use this, not (b)(4), for a worker standing on the top cap or top step. Ask: is this construction work (29 CFR 1926)? If no, use the general industry (1910) entry instead.

entries.requires: Employer uses either GFCIs as in (b)(1)(ii) or an assured equipment grounding conductor program as in (b)(1)(iii) to protect employees on construction sites
entries.note: Two ways to comply: no GFCI seen is not a violation if an assured equipment grounding conductor program is in place. Ask which one the employer uses. Ask: is this construction work (29 CFR 1926)? If no, use the general industry (1910) entry instead.

entries.note: Small two-wire generators (5 kW or less) with insulated conductors are exempt. Ask: is this construction work (29 CFR 1926)? If no, use the general industry (1910) entry instead.

entries.note: Ask: is this construction work (29 CFR 1926)? If no, use the general industry (1910) entry instead.

# Construction Site Safety Audit Report
Cover lines: CONFIDENTIAL · Client: [Client] · Project: [Project] · Site: [Site address] · General contractor: [GC] · Audit date(s): [Visit dates] · Report date: [Report date] · Report no.: [Report number] · Prepared for: [Site contact, only as given in writing]. Last cover line, label "Note": "This report reflects conditions observed on the audit date(s) only. It is not legal advice."
## 1. Audit Summary
Paragraph 1: who conducted the audit, at whose request and why, where and when, and the method (site walk, document review, interviews).
Paragraph 2: the result in one sentence using the app's numbers exactly: "[n] findings ([s] serious, [o] other-than-serious); overall score [x]% ([band] risk)." Say how many were corrected on site only if a source says so.
## 2. Scope and Method
Areas and activities walked, trades observed, documents reviewed, anything excluded. Then a table: Participant | Role (names only as given in writing).
## 3. Site Description
Project, phase and work under way, general contractor and trades on site, approximate workforce, weather and conditions. Two to four sentences from the job sheet only.
## 4. Overall Score
One sentence on the scale (each category rated Compliant, Minor Gap, Major Gap or Absent; Not Applicable left out; score is the average). -> a {"type":"scorecard"} block. Then one short paragraph naming the categories rated Absent or Major Gap.
## 5. Summary of Findings
-> a {"type":"counts"} block. One sentence on how many remain open.
## 6. Findings and Corrective Actions
Intro line: "Each finding gives the Condition, Requirement, Risk, Corrective action, Owner and Due date. Risk ratings are SERIOUS or OTHER-THAN-SERIOUS."
For each finding: F-[n] [Short title stating the condition] ([Risk rating]) with six labeled parts: Condition (what, where, exposing employer if known, evidence); Requirement (REGULATION – 29 CFR [cite from library]: [paraphrase]. Or SITE RULE – [document]: [rule].); Risk (one sentence); Corrective action (immediate action first, "(corrected on site)" only if a source says so, then the lasting fix); Owner (job title); Due date.
Recommendations (no citation): Rec-[n] [title] with Condition and Recommendation.
## 7. Corrective Action Plan
Table: # | Hazard | Location | Risk rating | Corrective action | Owner | Due date. One row per finding, same IDs.
## 8. Recommendations
Short bullets: program, training and supervision priorities, and a follow-up audit in [interval from the job sheet].
## 9. Limitations
Conditions on the audit date(s) only; a site walk may not find every hazard; each employer remains responsible for its employees' safety and for compliance; based on the areas, documents and people available.
styleRules:
Voice: third person, past tense for observations ("was blocked," "had been removed"). The firm is the subject in the summary ("[Firm] conducted…"), never "I" or "we."
Sentence length: short and plain, usually under 25 words. One idea per sentence.
Finding titles: state the condition, not the rule. Classification in parentheses. "– REPEAT" when the prior report recorded the same condition.
Finding structure: always six labeled parts, in order: Condition, Requirement, Risk, Corrective action, Owner, Due date.
Condition: exact item and location, then the evidence (observation, tag, log, document).
Requirement: label first (REGULATION or CLIENT POLICY), then the cite, then a plain-language paraphrase after a colon. No quoted regulation text.
Risk: one sentence, consequence-focused, no exaggeration.
Corrective action: start with a verb ("Remove," "Install," "Train," "Post"). Immediate step first; then the lasting fix. Owners are job titles, not names.
Numbers: numerals for counts and rates (two decimals for rates); dates as "March 4, 2026"; percentages as whole numbers unless the app gives a decimal.
Words avoided: "egregious," "blatant," "failed to," "it is recommended that," "please note," "ensure compliance."
Tables: scorecard in Section 4, counts in Section 5, corrective action plan in Section 7.
findingsLibrary:
Fall protection — Title: Unprotected edge at [level/area]. Requirement: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.501(b)(1): guardrails, safety nets or personal fall arrest at unprotected sides and edges 6 feet or more above a lower level. Risk: A worker could fall to the level below. Corrective action: Stop work at the edge, install guardrails, then add edge checks to the daily inspection.
Ladders — Title: Extension ladder not extended above the landing. Requirement: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.1053(b)(1): side rails extend at least 3 feet above the upper landing, or the ladder is secured and a grab device provided. Corrective action: Replace or reposition the ladder and secure it at the top.
Excavations — Title: No safe way out of the trench. Requirement: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.651(c)(2): stairway, ladder or ramp in trenches 4 feet or deeper within 25 feet of lateral travel. Corrective action: Place a ladder in the trench before anyone re-enters.
Silica — Title: Dry cutting of concrete. Requirement: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.1153(c)(1): Table 1 controls fully implemented for each listed task. Corrective action: Stop dry cutting; use a saw with integrated water delivery.
Impalement — Title: Uncapped rebar. Requirement: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.701(b): protruding reinforcing steel guarded against impalement. Corrective action: Cap or cover all exposed rebar ends.

blocks.text: The consultant conducted a site safety audit of the Maple Court Medical Office (sample) project on November 12, 2026, at the request of the Ridgeline Builders project manager as a quarterly third-party audit. The audit included a walk of the whole site, a review of site documents and interviews with the site superintendent and two trade foremen.
The audit identified 8 findings (6 serious, 2 other-than-serious); overall score 72.3% (Moderate risk). Five serious findings called for work to stop in the affected area until corrected.

The audit covered the whole site and all active trades. Crane work was excluded because no crane was on site. The consultant reviewed the site safety plan, the daily excavation inspection log for November 10 to 12, and the October toolbox talk sign-ins.

The project is a two-story steel-frame medical office building at 100 Demo Avenue, Sampleton. At the time of the audit the level 2 deck had been poured, interior wall framing was under way on level 1, and a storm drain trench was open on the north side. About 30 workers were on site from the general contractor and three trades. The weather was dry, 58°F, with light wind.
Each audit category is rated Compliant, Minor Gap, Major Gap or Absent; Not Applicable categories are left out. The overall score is the average across rated categories.
Fall protection, excavations and trenching, and health hazards (silica) were rated Major Gap. No category was rated Absent.
All 8 findings were open at the end of the audit.
Each finding gives the Condition, Requirement, Risk, Corrective action, Owner and Due date. Risk ratings are SERIOUS or OTHER-THAN-SERIOUS.

parts.text: Control joints were cut dry in the level 1 slab with a gas cut-off saw; no water was connected and a visible dust cloud was present (Level 1 slab; Concrete subcontractor). Evidence: site walk observation.

parts.label: Requirement
parts.text: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.1153(c)(1): For each Table 1 task, fully and properly implement the listed engineering controls, work practices and respiratory protection.

parts.label: Risk
parts.text: Workers and others nearby could breathe respirable crystalline silica.

parts.label: Corrective action
parts.text: Stop dry cutting. Use a saw with integrated water delivery, as Table 1 requires.

parts.label: Owner
parts.text: Concrete Foreman

parts.label: Due date
parts.text: November 12, 2026 (before cutting resumes)

blocks.title: Gasoline for the cut-off saw was kept in an unlabeled plastic jug

parts.label: Condition
parts.text: Gasoline for the cut-off saw was kept in an unlabeled plastic jug (Level 1 slab; Concrete subcontractor). Evidence: site walk observation.

parts.label: Requirement
parts.text: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.152(a)(1): Only approved containers and portable tanks; safety cans or DOT containers for 5 gallons or less.

parts.label: Risk
parts.text: An unapproved container can leak or be mistaken for another liquid and increases fire risk.

parts.label: Corrective action
parts.text: Move the fuel to an approved, labeled safety can.

parts.label: Owner
parts.text: Concrete Foreman

parts.label: Due date
parts.text: November 13, 2026

blocks.title: About 12 rebar dowels along the elevator pit wall were uncapped

parts.label: Condition
parts.text: About 12 rebar dowels along the elevator pit wall were uncapped (Elevator pit; Concrete subcontractor). Evidence: site walk observation.

parts.label: Requirement
parts.text: REGULATION – 29 CFR 1926.701(b): Protruding reinforcing steel guarded to eliminate the hazard of impalement.

parts.label: Risk
parts.text: A worker who falls onto an uncapped dowel could be impaled.

parts.label: Corrective action
parts.text: Cap or cover all exposed rebar ends at the elevator pit.

parts.label: Owner
parts.text: Concrete Foreman

parts.label: Due date
parts.text: November 13, 2026

blocks.title: Silica training reached most, but not all, of the concrete crew

parts.label: Condition
parts.text: The October silica toolbox talk sign-in lists 9 of the 11 concrete crew members.

parts.label: Recommendation
parts.text: Repeat the silica talk for the 2 crew members not on the sign-in by December 1, 2026.
